policy_title: Provide tax relief for independent education
stated: Reform UK will introduce 20% tax relief on all independent education and abolish VAT on fees, aiming to incentivise parents to choose independent schools and ease pressure on state schools.

source.quote: Tax relief of 20% on all Independent Education No VAT on Fees. If parents can afford to pay a bit more, we should incentivise them to choose independent schools. This will significantly ease pressure on state schools and improve education for all.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly reshapes the state/independent school balance — affecting state-school capacity and funding dynamics, the attainment gap, and who can access different types of schooling — earning a real verdict on education and opportunity.

Abolishing VAT on fees and adding 20% tax relief is a concrete tax change that reduces the financial burden on families paying private school fees, directly affecting take-home value for those households.

Removing VAT on independent school fees reverses significant revenue (OBR/HM Treasury modelled the Labour VAT addition at ~£1.5bn/yr), and the additional 20% tax relief creates a further revenue cost, materially widening the funding gap.

The financial benefits flow overwhelmingly to higher-income households who can afford private school fees even after relief, plausibly widening the income and opportunity gap between those households and lower-income families with no access to the scheme.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn a genuine verdict: the education allocation effect (O7), the direct tax-cut gain (O11), the material revenue cost to public finances (O12), and the regressive distributional profile of the benefit (O14). No credible non-negligible mechanism connects this policy to crime/security, healthcare, housing, environment, later-life security, or liberty indicators.
